rows.subtype: Stage 4: First payment and sunk cost [Response]
rows.description: A person who realises they have already paid stops, screenshots the messages and talks to a bank and a trusted adult. Accepting the first loss is cheaper than chasing it with more money.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.description: The victim is told to act now, tell nobody and stay on the line, with threats of arrest or loss of a rare chance. Pressure and isolation shut down the slower thinking that would spot the problem.
graph_context: next stage: First payment and sunk cost
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: loneliness

rows.subtype: Stage 4: First payment and sunk cost [Receiver]
rows.description: After a first small transfer, the victim feels committed and pays more to recover what is already lost. The wish to avoid admitting a mistake becomes the manipulator's best tool.
graph_context: previous stage: Urgency and secrecy
next stage: Doubt and denial
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Inconsistencies appear, and part of the victim knows something is wrong but hopes it is not. Fear of shame, family reaction and loss of face makes it hard to tell anyone.
graph_context: previous stage: First payment and sunk cost
next stage: Breaking out
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: fear, shame, doubt, hope

rows.description: A family member sees odd secrecy, rushed transfers and a person glued to their phone. Asking calmly, with no blame, and suggesting a pause to verify through an official channel can break the spell.
graph_context: previous stage: First payment and sunk cost
next stage: Breaking out
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: doubt, calm

rows.description: The victim stops payment, hangs up, checks through the official number or app, and tells a trusted person. Reporting quickly to the bank and the cybercrime helpline gives the best chance to limit harm.
graph_context: previous stage: Doubt and denial
next stage: Shame and recovery
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: detachment, trust

rows.description: Afterwards the victim feels foolish and angry. Friends and family who treat it as a crime against the person, not a stupidity, help them recover and share the story so others can spot the pattern.
graph_context: previous stage: Breaking out
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: anger, shame

rows.description: A child is not picked for a game or a birthday and feels a sharp ache of not belonging. The hurt is big and personal, and they may not have words for it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: nostalgia, hurt

rows.description: A teenager stops texting first, skips gatherings and says they prefer being alone. Withdrawal protects from further rejection but also removes the chance of connection.
graph_context: previous stage: Feeling left out
next stage: Reading signals as rejection
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: detachment

rows.description: A lonely mind scans for threat, so a late reply or a laugh is taken to mean dislike. This bias makes the person more guarded and awkward, and confirms the fear.
graph_context: previous stage: Protective pulling back
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, fear, embarrassment, loneliness
